verdict.rationale: Neon documents a dedicated Scale to Zero capability and states that idle databases incur no ongoing compute overhead. It also offers a free tier with no time limits and separates storage from compute, and a community user praises paying only for calls on a hobby project. However, the scale-to-zero docs appear in the pack only as a title, and durability of data while compute is suspended is only implied by the storage/compute separation. missing for 10: substantive first-party detail on scale-to-zero behavior (idle timeout, suspend/resume), explicit documentation that data persists durably while compute is at zero, explicit confirmation that idle prototypes incur zero cost (community notes a $20 minimum entry cost on paid plans), hands-on corroboration of suspend/resume.

support.subject: As a founder, idle databases scale to zero so prototypes and side projects cost nothing while the data stays durable

citations.quote: because Neon resources are ephemeral by design, idle databases don't incur ongoing compute overhead.
Neon is an open-source serverless Postgres database platform. It separates storage and compute
Build and learn free with no time limits and no credit card required.
Having a relational database where you're charged purely for the calls you make is a game-changer.
